sectionSubtitle: Analyze static performance issues and the game's error.log without launching the game. Every finding links to the entity that caused it.
perfSubtitle: Scans your focus trees, events, decisions, ideas and characters for script that the game re-evaluates too often (scope loops in hot contexts, oversized files, polled timers with no floor).
perfClean: No performance smells found. Nothing the game would re-evaluate too often.
perfScanned: Scanned {focusNodes} focuses · {events} events · {decisions} decisions · {ideas} ideas · {characters} characters
perfFailed: Could not run the performance scan: {err}
logSubtitle: Upload the error.log the game writes after a crash or load (logs/error.log). Every line is classified and linked to the entity it concerns.
logEmptyHelper: After a crash or load, HOI4 writes a logs/error.log. Upload it, and every line gets classified and linked to the entity it concerns.
logClean: No errors in this log. Your last game session loaded cleanly.
logNotRecognized: This doesn't look like a HOI4 error.log (expected logs/error.log format) — nothing was read. Pick the file at Documents/Paradox Interactive/Hearts of Iron IV/logs/error.log.
logSummary: {unique} unique errors from {lines} lines · {mapped} linked to an entity
logTooLarge: That file is too large (max 25 MB).
unmappedEntity: Could not link this to a specific entity
findingsTruncated: +{count} more in this group. Fix the ones listed above first, then re-scan.
logVerdictClean: No script errors that would crash the game. The other {n} are mostly known noise / from another mod.
logVerdictIssues: Found {k} script error(s) worth fixing; the other {m} are mostly harmless.
bucketGroup_D_bug5_fixed_hint: These can stop the game from reading your files — worth fixing.
bucketGroup_C_gap_hint: File types the editor doesn't model yet — kept as-is on export, usually nothing to do.
bucketGroup_D_triage_tail_hint: Usually inherent to the mod; known and safe to ignore.
bucketGroup_D_unknown_hint: Not recognized. Usually harmless, or from another mod or version differences.
bucketGroup_mod_noise_hint: Font line-height / DLC checks and the like — safe to ignore.
perfCode_nested_scope_loop_title: Nested scope loop (O(N²)) in a hot context
perfCode_nested_scope_loop_suggestion: Cache the outer result in a variable, narrow the inner set with a `limit` block, or move the work behind a one-shot triggered event instead of a polled context.
perfCode_nested_scope_loop_coldpath_sugg: Narrow the inner set with a `limit` block or restructure to avoid iterating all scopes twice.
perfCode_hot_scope_loop_title: Scope loop in a frequently-evaluated context
perfCode_hot_scope_loop_suggestion: Prefer a cheap pre-check before the loop, gate the context with `is_triggered_only` / a flag, or add a `days = N` floor so it polls less often.
perfCode_heavy_trigger_fanout_title: Heavy trigger fan-out in a hot context
perfCode_heavy_trigger_fanout_suggestion: Split the check, short-circuit with the cheapest condition first, or precompute the result into a flag updated on a slower cadence.
perfCode_mtth_no_floor_title: Polled event MTTH has no base interval
perfCode_mtth_no_floor_suggestion: Add a base `days = N` (or `months`/`years`) so the engine polls less often, or make the event `is_triggered_only` and fire it explicitly.
perfCode_expensive_available_recheck_tit: Database-wide check re-runs on every UI refresh
perfCode_expensive_available_recheck_sug: If the value rarely changes, cache it in a country variable updated on a slower cadence and compare the variable here instead.
perfCode_oversized_focus_tree_suggestion: Split shared branches into a `shared_focus` pool or a second tree, or gate late-game branches behind `allow_branch` so they don't all load eagerly.
perfCode_oversized_event_file_suggestion: Split the namespace into themed sub-namespaces so each generated event file stays small and editable.
perfCode_oversized_decision_category_sug: Group decisions into more categories so fewer are evaluated/visible at once, and gate rarely-relevant ones behind a category `visible` trigger.
perfCode_total_focus_weight_title: Project has a very large number of focuses
perfCode_total_focus_weight_suggestion: Consider whether all trees need to load for every country, and lean on shared pools where branches repeat.
playtestSubtitle: Drop in what HOI4 wrote when you launched. It catches what export can't see: a wrong start date, a crash, or a mod load-order conflict.
playtestClean: No playtest issues found — the start date, load order and crash log look clean.
playtestEmptyHelper: Pick any of logs/game.log, dlc_load.json, or crashes/[timestamp]/exception.txt from your Documents/Paradox Interactive/Hearts of Iron IV folder, then Analyze.
timelineSubtitle: Checks that your project start date, scenario bookmarks and any hand-written defines file all agree — a mismatch makes the game start on a date you didn't mean.
timelineFailed: Could not run the timeline check: {err}
timelineFollowsVanilla: No start date set — the mod follows the vanilla / base-mod start date, so there is nothing to check. You can set one in project settings.
timelineCode_bookmark_date_mismatch_titl: Bookmark date differs from the project start date
timelineCode_bookmark_date_mismatch_reas: Bookmark "{id}" starts at {bookmarkDate}, but the project start date is {startDate}. The player enters the game at the bookmark's date, not the project's.
timelineCode_bookmark_date_mismatch_sugg: Set the bookmark's date and the project start date to the same day so the scenario and the game start date agree.
timelineCode_no_bookmark_for_custom_star: Custom start date but no scenario bookmark

The project starts at {startDate}, but it defines no bookmark. The vanilla 1936 / 1939 scenarios will still appear on the country-select screen, and picking one runs history written for 1936 — not your timeline.
Create a bookmark dated {startDate}; the export will then hide the vanilla scenarios automatically.
timelineCode_defines_conflict_title: Hand-written defines file sets a different start date
timelineCode_defines_conflict_reason: This raw file sets the game start date to {definesDate}, but the project start date is {startDate}. On export the raw file wins, so the game would start at {definesDate}.
timelineCode_defines_conflict_suggestion: Make the two dates agree: update the raw defines file, or change the project start date to match it.
timelineCode_defines_manual_title: Raw defines file sets a start date the project doesn't know about
timelineCode_defines_manual_reason: A raw defines file sets the game start date to {definesDate}, but the project start date field is empty.
timelineCode_defines_manual_suggestion: Set the project start date to {definesDate} too, so validation and AI guidance line up with what the mod actually does.
timelineCode_empty_bookmarks_replace_tit: replace_path would empty the bookmarks folder
timelineCode_empty_bookmarks_replace_rea: A raw file opts into replace_path for common/bookmarks, but this export ships no bookmark. The game would replace the vanilla bookmarks folder with an empty one — no selectable scenario, broken campaign start.
timelineCode_empty_bookmarks_replace_sug: Add a bookmark (or a bookmark .txt raw file), or turn off the replace_path option on that raw file.
timelineCode_vanilla_bookmarks_hidden_ti: Export will hide the vanilla 1936 / 1939 scenarios
timelineCode_vanilla_bookmarks_hidden_re: This project uses a custom start date and ships its own bookmark, so the export automatically replaces the bookmarks folder — only your scenarios will appear in-game.
timelineCode_start_date_ok_reason: Project start date {startDate}, bookmarks and defines all agree.
playtestRuntimeSubtitle: Add the files HOI4 wrote during launch to check the loaded scenario, active environment, expected mod identity and last reached lifecycle stage.
playtestExpectedIdentityHelper: Name and descriptor path work as a pair. Add the optional build ID when the artifact contains one; a name match alone never proves a duplicate.
playtestRuntimeDlcEnvironmentOnly: The DLC count describes this launch environment only. It does not tell the mod to disable or bypass DLC checks.
playtestIdentityActivated: The inventory marks the exact expected name, path and build identity as active.
playtestIdentityNotActivated: The supplied evidence says the expected mod was not activated. This is not evidence of a duplicate name.
playtestIdentityCollision: The inventory proves that more than one descriptor uses the same normalized name and path.
playtestIdentityIndeterminate: The available evidence cannot prove whether the exact expected identity was active.
playtestChronologyEvidenceHelper: This is simply the last non-empty line observed. It can show where logging stopped, but it does not identify why the game stopped.
playtestNoIssueFound: No issue was identified in the supplied evidence. This diagnostic result is not proof that the mod is game-safe.
playtestRuntimeEmptyHelper: Choose any of logs/game.log, logs/system.log, dlc_load.json, crashes/[timestamp]/exception.txt or a launcher mod-inventory JSON file, then analyze.
